page: Microsoft Azure D8_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dv3 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware configuration features an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It supports AVX, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets, but lacks AVX-512 capabilities. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes a bundled 205 GB local SSD for storage, but does not feature any GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the D8_v3 operates primarily in the lower performance tiers. Single-core CPU performance is positioned in the bottom 10%, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 775.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 824.0. Multi-core performance falls into the bottom 25%, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3648.3 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3184.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block speeds at 36.83 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 21.43 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom 25%. However, the server demonstrates average performance in text generation for small language models (135M), achieving 85.57 tokens/sec, though prompt processing for the same model remains in the bottom 25% at 220.66 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8_v3 offers a standard general-purpose resource density with a balanced CPU-to-memory ratio, making it a predictable option for workloads that do not require high-performance compute or high-speed memory throughput. Given the lower benchmark scores in database operations (2151.27 on PassMark) and static web serving (4.87 GB/sec), this server is best suited for light general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, development environments, and small-scale background processing tasks where raw computational speed is not a critical requirement.
